case_title: Dr. Vinod Bhandari v. State of M.P.
accused_occupation: Managing Director of a medical institute (Shri Aurbindo Institute of Medical Sciences, Indore)
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.420, 467, 468, 471, 120B; Madhya Pradesh Manyata Prapt Pariksha Adhiniyam 1937 s.3(d), 1, 2/4; Information Technology Act ss.65, 66 (as listed in FIR)
evidence_type: Documentary (excel data from seized hard disc, seized Vyapam documents, seized candidate list, cash seizure memo); recovery on co-accused's disclosure; s.164 CrPC statement of another person. Cited by the High Court, not tested by the Supreme Court.
confession: None by the accused. A co-accused's disclosure statement and another person's s.164 CrPC statement were cited by the State; the Court made no finding on their reliance.
aggravating_circumstances: High magnitude (large number of undeserving admissions by corrupt means); serious adverse impact on society; alleged depravity of character and black money generation; alleged kingpin role; alleged potential to influence witnesses.
trial_court_outcome: No verdict; second bail application dismissed by the 9th Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal on 9 May 2014 (trial not concluded)
high_court_outcome: Division Bench dismissed the bail application (order dated 11.08.2014 in M.Cr.C. No. 10371 of 2014)
neutral_facts: Officers of a state examination board and middlemen allegedly arranged copying in a 2012 pre-medical entrance examination so that candidates who paid money could gain admission to MBBS courses. The prosecution alleges that the accused, who headed a medical institute, passed money through his general manager to a systems analyst at the board who held the model answer key, and part of the money reached the board's controller. Investigators allege that high-scoring candidates were seated at the examination centre, that OMR sheets were left blank and later filled with correct answers, and that the answer key was given to candidates one night before the examination. A co-accused's disclosure statement reportedly led to the recovery of cash and documents. The prosecution relies on a certified copy of an excel sheet retrieved from a hard disc seized from the systems analyst's office, documents and activity charts seized from the board, a list of 150 candidates seized from the institute for the 2012-13 MBBS session, and a seizure memo for cash taken from the general manager. It is alleged that seven candidates sponsored by the accused were passed by filling OMR circles with the analyst's connivance. A section 164 statement by another doctor reportedly says he was asked to pay 20 lakh rupees, through the general manager, for his son's admission.
offence_severity: Life sentence (as stated in the High Court order quoted in the judgment; no other range stated)
number_of_offences: 10 sections listed in FIR (charge framing not stated); 0 finally upheld (no conviction decided)
financial_property_loss: Alleged: appellant received few crores of rupees; 60 lakh rupees cash seized from general manager (per High Court material)
premeditation_planning: Not decided by the Court; prosecution material describes a 'well designed conspiracy'
motive: alleged: monetary gain from arranging admission of undeserving candidates
key_evidence_accepted: No merits findings; Court accepted at prima facie level that allegations are supported by material on record (excel data, seized documents, candidate list, seizure memo)
post_offence_conduct: Noted by the High Court (not a Supreme Court finding): went abroad soon after registration of the crime and returned only after anticipatory bail was granted
custody_duration: About one year in custody (arrested 30 January 2014, per the judgment)
bail_history: Anticipatory bail granted in other FIR on 16 Jan 2014; first bail application dismissed 5 Feb 2014; second dismissed 9 May 2014; High Court dismissed bail 11 Aug 2014; Supreme Court directed the appellant may apply afresh if trial not completed within one year
trial_duration: offence: 2012 (PMT Examination; FIR registered 30 October 2013); trial judgment: not given (no trial judgment, bail matter only); High Court: 11.08.2014; Supreme Court: 04.02.2015
legal_representation: Accused: Siddharth Luthra, H. P. Raval, Kunal Verma, Keki Vajpei, Prasanna Mohan, Anando Mukherjee. State: Mishra Saurabh, Vanshaja Shukla, Ankit Kr. Lal
investigation_status: FIR registered 30 October 2013; 329 arrested and 187 to be arrested out of 516 accused; charge sheets filed; final charge sheet directed by 15 March 2015
appeal_history: Trial court (9th Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal): bail refused 9 May 2014. High Court (Division Bench): bail dismissed 11 Aug 2014. Supreme Court: appeal disposed of; liberty to apply afresh for bail if trial not completed within one year for reasons not attributable to the appellant
prosecution_argument: Courts below considered nature of allegations, material, likelihood of misuse of bail and impact on society; clear prima facie complicity; offence punishable with life; appellant was kingpin; potential to influence witnesses; investigation pending; appellant earlier went abroad
defence_argument: About one year in custody with no prospect of early trial; 516 accused and many witnesses and documents mean a long trial; investigation not complete; prolonged custody entitles appellant to bail
legal_principle_applied: Bail is for ensuring availability for trial, not punishment; seriousness is not the sole test; delay in trial is a relevant factor; prima facie material and potential to influence trial are considered; prosecution and court must ensure speedy trial
precedent_relied_upon: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan (2005) 2 SCC 42; State of U.P. v. Amarmani Tripathi (2005) 8 SCC 21; State of Kerala v. Raneef (2011) 1 SCC 784; Sanjay Chandra v. CBI (2012) 1 SCC 40
judicial_aggravating_factors: Serious adverse impact on society; high magnitude; depravity of character; black money generation; undermining trust in medical profession; potential of trial being adversely influenced by bail
other_sentence_order: Directions: trial to proceed day to day; High Court to review progress once in three months; appellant may apply afresh for bail if trial not completed within one year for reasons not attributable to him; observations are not an opinion on merits
